To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the chicken Bestrophin channel is activated by calcium and inactivated by the inactivation peptide, and that both activation and inactivation are allosteric processes that involve rearrangement of a neck of the ion pore.

Bestrophin is a novel class of ligand-gated anion channel, and that it has a unique molecular mechanism for gating that is based on the repositioning and rotation of pore-lining helical segments within an otherwise stable protein shell.

the bestrophin family of ligand-gated anion-selective ion channels are opened by calcium binding to a site that is allosterically linked to the opening of a neck of the channel pore, and that the pore is closed by a peptide that binds to the neck and induces a conformational change that closes the neck.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of gating in ion channels.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate ion transport through membrane channels and transporters.
the molecular mechanisms of ion channel gating.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cryo-EM structure reveals a novel mechanism for gating in which a neck of the ion pore is the gate and that Ca2+ binding opens the pore by a concerted movement of helices within the surrounding protein shell, and the inactivation peptide closes the pore by binding to a site within the neck of the pore.
the cryo-EM structures of chicken BEST-1 presented by this group provide a molecular mechanism for activation and inactivation of a calcium-gated chloride channel.
bestrophins are ligand-gated anion channels with a gating mechanism that is distinct from other ligand-gated channels.

we have solved the structures of the chicken BEST1 channel at 3.2-3.4Å resolution and that we have determined how the channel is activated by Ca2+.
